research_metadata.method: z-ai web_search CLI (commercial pricing) + GitHub Search API (unauthenticated, 10/min burst limit) + curated knowledge for well-trodden patterns
research_metadata.rate_limit_notes: GitHub core API exhausted (60/hr unauth, 1 remaining); search API used in 2 parallel batches. Web search CLI rate-limited at ~3 req/min — used serial calls with sleep(3) between.

B18.name: Job board API rate limit management
B18.description: Quota tracking, key rotation, backoff, and fallback across job board APIs with disparate quotas (JSearch 200/mo, Adzuna 250/day 1000/wk 2500/mo, USAJobs ~1000/hr).

oss_tools.desc: Async token-bucket rate limiter for asyncio. Use one limiter per API per key.
Retry/backoff library. Pair with aiolimiter to handle 429s with exponential + jitter.
Async HTTP client with first-class transport adapters — write a quota-tracking transport.

commercial_services.pricing: JSearch BASIC free 200 req/mo; PRO $25/mo for 10,000 + $0.003 overage
commercial_services.desc: RapidAPI itself manages key rotation if you add multiple keys to your project dashboard.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Per-provider wrapper class: (1) KeyPool[provider] holds N API keys; (2) Limiter enforces both RPM and daily/monthly caps via aiolimiter + a SQLite counters table; (3) httpx AsyncBaseTransport subclass wraps each call — on 429/403 it marks key as 'cooling' for Retry-After seconds and rotates to next key; (4) Fallback chain: if all keys exhausted, route to a slower free source (e.g., USAJobs for govt jobs, Remotive RSS for remote). Emit prometheus-style metrics. Persist counters in tracker DB so restarts don't lose quota state.

recommendation.why: Quota semantics differ per provider (RPM vs RPD vs RPM-with-cooldown), so generic SaaS can't model the rules — a thin per-provider wrapper using aiolimiter is the standard pattern. Total ~10 dev-days.

B19.name: Cross-time content-fingerprint dedup
B19.description: Same job reposted weeks later with new ID and slightly edited text. Need dedup that survives reposting, beyond URL/title match.

oss_tools.desc: Charikar's simhash for near-duplicate detection. Hamming-distance ≤ 3 considered duplicate.
MinHash + LSH. Scales to millions of docs; supports Jaccard threshold tuning.
Embed JD with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, cosine sim ≥ 0.92 = near-dup. Best for semantically-edited reposts.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Two-stage filter: (1) BLOCK = normalize(company_name) + normalize(title) + location + salary_band (if present) → fast SHA-256 shortlist for exact reposts; (2) FUZZY = minhash of normalized JD tokens (strip dates, IDs, recruiter names) stored in LSH index → candidate set; (3) SEMANTIC = sentence-transformers embedding cosine sim on candidates to catch LLM-rewritten reposts. Store all three hashes in jobs table; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT by simhash bucket. Run dedup at ingestion time, surface 'possibly-reposted-from: <job_id>' on tracker UI.

recommendation.best_commercial: none (no SaaS specifically for job-repost dedup)
recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: BLOCK hash + datasketch minhash + sentence-transformers for borderline cases
recommendation.why: datasketch is purpose-built for near-dup at scale; pure URL/title dedup misses 60-70% of reposts. Add embeddings only when minhash is ambiguous — keeps cost low.

B20.name: Company hiring season / cycle detection
B20.description: Some companies hire in predictable batches (new grad Q3, Q1 budget refresh, seasonal retail). Detect patterns from historical postings.

oss_tools.desc: SARIMA / seasonal decomposition (STL) — textbook tool for monthly hiring counts per company.
Additive model with built-in seasonality detection + holidays. Easiest 'fit and forecast' API.
Online learning — adapt seasonal model as new postings arrive without re-batch.

commercial_services.desc: Workforce analytics — useful for hiring-trend validation, not for personal pipeline.

build_it_yourself.architecture: For each company with ≥12 months of postings: monthly count time-series → STL decomposition → store seasonal_strength + peak_month in company_hiring_pattern table. Surface in tracker UI as 'peak hiring: March (3yr avg)' badge. Prophet is overkill for personal use; STL via statsmodels is ~30 lines. Trigger weekly batch over companies seen >5 times.
build_it_yourself.estimated_effort: 1-2 days (1 dev). Needs ≥6 months historical data per company for any signal.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: monthly bucket counts + STL via statsmodels
recommendation.why: This is a personal tracker, not enterprise workforce analytics — STL over your own jobs table is the right-sized tool. Prophet needs more data than individuals typically have.

M15.name: Secret management
M15.description: Secure storage for API keys, LinkedIn cookies, OAuth tokens, etc.

oss_tools.desc: Mozilla SOPS — encrypt values in YAML/JSON, leave keys visible. age/KMS/PGP backends. Git-friendly (diffable).
Open-source HashiCorp Vault alternative with a CLI, SDKs, K8s injector, and self-host option. Free for 5 identities.
Industry standard secret manager. Overkill for single-user but supports dynamic secrets + leases.
Simple file encryption tool. Pair with a passphrase or YubiKey. The minimal primitive SOPS uses.

commercial_services.desc: Fully managed secret manager with good DX (CLI + dashboards). Closed source.
Hosted Infisical. Same UI as OSS but no ops burden.
General-purpose password managers with CLI + 'op run' / 'bw get' for secret injection. Great for cookies + API keys.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Store secrets.yaml in repo, encrypted with SOPS+age. CI/dev runs `sops exec-env secrets.yaml -- python main.py`. age key kept in OS keychain (macOS: `security`, Linux: `secret-tool`, Win: DPAPI). For LinkedIn cookies with expiry, store expiry_ts alongside and rotate via hook. ~1 file, ~2 hours.

recommendation.why: For a personal project, SOPS+age wins on simplicity and audit trail (commits show which key changed). Doppler wins for teams that want zero ops. Vault is overkill unless you need dynamic DB creds.

M16.name: Data backup / export
M16.description: Tracker DB, profile, and resumes should be exportable and backup-friendly.

oss_tools.desc: sqlite3 `.backup` API does online consistent snapshot of WAL-mode DB without locking writers. Standard.
Continuous SQLite WAL streaming to S3/GCS/Azure. Sub-second RPO. Single-binary install.
Encrypted, deduplicated, incremental backups to many backends. Use for the whole repo (resumes, configs, DB snapshots).

commercial_services.pricing: Free for public repos; private 2000 min/mo free
commercial_services.desc: Nightly SQLite .backup → CSV/JSON export → commit to a private backup branch. Zero infra.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Two layers: (1) CONTINUOUS = litestream replicate sqlite.db to S3 (RPO ~1s); (2) NIGHTLY = `sqlite3 tracker.db .backup /backup/tracker-YYYYMMDD.db` + dump each table to CSV + JSON, tar with resume PDFs, encrypt with age, push to git branch 'backup' and S3. Retain 90 daily + 12 monthly. ~50 lines shell.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: sqlite3 .backup nightly + restic to S3 free tier
recommendation.why: Litestream covers the 'I just lost my disk' case with near-zero RPO; restic handles snapshots + resume PDFs. Both OSS, no SaaS dependency.

M17.name: Multi-device sync
M17.description: Edit tracker from laptop, phone, desktop. Conflict-free merge.

oss_tools.desc: P2P continuous file sync. No central server. Best for syncing the SQLite DB file + resume PDFs across machines.
CRDT for collaborative editing. If tracker is web-based, use yjs for live multi-user edits on the same record.
JSON CRDT. Good for structured record sync. Rust core (y-crdt port) gives Python bindings.
Causal CRDT layer for SQLite — each row becomes a CRDT. Native SQLite, multi-writer sync without conflicts.

commercial_services.desc: Hosted SQLite at the edge — sync via HTTP instead of file replication. Per-device local cache.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Three options ordered by complexity: (EASY) Syncthing for the tracker's SQLite file (single-writer-at-a-time via advisory lock — fine for one user across 3 devices). (MED) cr-sqlite — register tables as crsql, peer-sync via libp2p or simple HTTP relay. (HARD) Move tracker to a Turso DB and have each device connect directly. For a personal tracker, EASY is sufficient.
build_it_yourself.estimated_effort: EASY: 30 min; MED: 2 days; HARD: 3-5 days

recommendation.best_oss: syncthing (file-level) — for a personal single-user tracker
recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: syncthing + SQLite WAL + advisory lock
recommendation.why: A personal tracker is single-writer most of the time — Syncthing's file-level sync is enough and adds zero code. Only escalate to cr-sqlite if you actually need concurrent edits.

M18.name: Audit log / pipeline run observability
M18.description: Who did what when — for debugging scrapers, scoring, and apply-bot runs.

oss_tools.desc: Zero-config structured logging. `logger.add('runs.log', serialize=True)` = JSON log. Best DX for solo devs.
Structured logging with processors (bind context = run_id, scraper_name, etc.). More ceremony than loguru, scales better.
Distributed tracing — spans for each scraper/score/apply step. Export to Jaeger/Grafana Tempo.

commercial_services.desc: Best-in-class observability for pipeline tracing. Free tier generous for personal use.
Loki + Tempo + Prometheus in one stack.

build_it_yourself.architecture: loguru with a structured sink: each run gets UUID, all logs carry {run_id, stage, scraper, target}. Emit to JSONL file rotated daily. Add a tiny `runs` table in tracker DB: (run_id, started_at, ended_at, status, error). Postgres/SQLite queryable for 'show me last 10 scraper failures'. OTel is overkill until you have >5 services.

recommendation.why: OTel is right answer for distributed systems but adds real overhead. loguru with structured JSON output + a runs table in your existing SQLite covers 90% of debugging needs in <50 LOC.

M19.name: Rate limiting / throttling
M19.description: Don't hammer job boards or your own services.

oss_tools.desc: Asyncio-native async token bucket. Compose with httpx for clean rate-limited client.
Redis module implementing GCRA rate limit. Single INCR-like command. Best when you have Redis already.
FastAPI/Starlette rate limiting middleware. Use if you expose tracker as a web API.

commercial_services.desc: Edge rate limiting on the CDN — only relevant if you expose a public API.
Serverless rate limiting on Upstash Redis. REST API, multi-region.

build_it_yourself.architecture: For scrapers (egress limiting): aiolimiter(AsyncLimiter(1, 2)) = 0.5 req/sec per host, wrap in httpx transport. For tracker API (ingress limiting): slowapi on FastAPI routes. Redis only if multi-process; otherwise in-memory counter dict is fine.

recommendation.why: You're a single process — no need for distributed rate limiting. aiolimiter is 50 LOC and integrates with any httpx-based client. Escalate to redis-cell only when multi-worker.

M20.name: Proxy / IP rotation
M20.description: For scrapers that need IP rotation (LinkedIn, ATSs with bot detection).

oss_tools.desc: Scrapy middleware that rotates from a proxy list, bans dead proxies, retries on errors.
Crawls free proxy sources, validates, serves via HTTP API. Quality of free proxies is low — use for benign scraping only.
Python HTTP client with TLS fingerprint impersonation (Chrome/Safari). Often bypasses Cloudflare without proxies — try this first.

commercial_services.pricing: Residential $4.00/GB pay-as-you-go, $3.50/GB at $499 plan, $1.40/GB at volume
commercial_services.desc: Largest proxy pool (175M+ IPs), good docs, best for hard targets (LinkedIn).
Premium enterprise alternative to Bright Data. Better US/EU coverage.
Best value provider — pay per IP rather than per GB for sticky residential.
All-in-one scraping API that handles proxy rotation + retry + CAPTCHA routing. Best for 'I don't want to manage proxies'.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Skip proxies entirely until you actually get blocked — first try (1) curl-cffi with TLS impersonation, (2) Playwright stealth, (3) request rate < 0.5 req/sec with jittered delays, (4) only then add a paid residential pool. Self-rolled free proxies (proxy_pool) yield <30% success on real targets — usually wasted time.
build_it_yourself.estimated_effort: 0 days if curl-cffi works; 1-2 days integrating Bright Data SDK if not

recommendation.best_oss: curl-cffi (often avoids need for proxies entirely)
recommendation.best_commercial: Bright Data for hard targets / Decodo for value / ScraperAPI for no-ops
recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: curl-cffi + jittered delays + Playwright stealth
recommendation.why: Most personal-scraping blocks are TLS-fingerprint-based, not IP-based — curl-cffi solves 70% of cases for free. Save paid proxies for LinkedIn-scale targets.

M21.name: CAPTCHA solving
M21.description: Solve reCAPTCHA / hCaptcha / Turnstile / image CAPTCHAs for sites that need it.

oss_tools.desc: CapMonster Cloud Python SDK — same API as 2captcha.

commercial_services.desc: Oldest service, supports all CAPTCHA types. ~3-15s solve time.
AI-based solver, faster and slightly cheaper. Good Turnstile/hCaptcha support.
Long-running competitor, decent reliability.
ZennoLab's API — good for self-hosted option (CapMonster Lite runs locally).

build_it_yourself.architecture: Don't build a solver — these services exist because CV + ML is expensive and laborious. Wrap 2captcha + CapSolver behind a Provider interface, fall back from primary → secondary. Cache solutions per (site, captcha_image_hash) for 1 hour — often same site shows same CAPTCHA to multiple sessions briefly. Watch spend — at $1/1000, careless scraping can rack up $50/day on a tough target.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: avoid CAPTCHA by using authenticated APIs where possible (USAJobs/Remotive have no CAPTCHA; LinkedIn logged-in has no CAPTCHA)
recommendation.why: CAPTCHA solving is commodity-priced (sub-cent per solve). Don't roll your own. But first ask if you can avoid the CAPTCHA site entirely via a different source.

M22.name: Headless browser service
M22.description: Run Playwright/Puppeteer in a container without a local display.

oss_tools.desc: Self-hostable Chrome-as-a-service. Docker image, WebSocket CDP endpoint. v2 (browserless/chrome) is current OSS fork.
Playwright integration for Scrapy. Manage browser context per-spider, render pages, handle JS.
Official Playwright Python bindings. Run `playwright install chromium` once and you're set for headless.

commercial_services.pricing: Free (1 hr + 1 concurrent); Developer $20/mo (100 hrs); Startup $99/mo
commercial_services.desc: Managed headless Chrome with built-in stealth, CAPTCHA handling, session reuse, observability dashboards.
Same engine as OSS, hosted. Direct CDP endpoint.
Serverless actors marketplace — wrap Playwright scripts, run on schedule, store results.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Two options: (LOCAL) Just install Playwright Python + `playwright install chromium`. Headless works on Linux without X server via bundled libs. Add xvfb-run only if a site complains. (SERVER) Run `docker run -p 3000:3000 browserless/chrome` and connect via CDP from your scraper. Browserbase only worth it if you need stealth + CAPTCHA handling baked in.
build_it_yourself.estimated_effort: 0 days (local Playwright); 0.5 day (self-hosted browserless in Docker)

recommendation.why: For a personal scraper running locally, plain `playwright install` is enough. Browserbase is the right escalation when stealth becomes the bottleneck.

H12.name: Multi-stage interview tracking
H12.description: Phone screen → onsite → offer, with dates and notes per stage.

oss_tools.desc: Most are commercial/SaaS; OSS alternatives are basic. Self-rolled SQLite schema is the de-facto answer.

commercial_services.desc: Visual pipeline kanban for applications with custom stages + notes per stage. Closest to spec.
Job tracker + resume builder. Stages + contacts + notes.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Three tables: applications(id, company, role, status, source_id, applied_at); interview_stages(id, application_id, stage_type, scheduled_at, completed_at, outcome, notes, participants); stage_types enum [phone_screen, recruiter_call, technical, onsite, team_match, offer, rejected]. UI: timeline view per application. Add trigger to bump application.status when stage outcome = 'passed'. ~50 LOC + a Flask/Streamlit UI.

recommendation.best_oss: none dominant — self-rolled SQLite is the pattern
recommendation.why: Schema is trivial (~5 columns per stage) and tightly coupled to your existing tracker — extending your SQLite is faster than integrating an external app. Huntr is the right answer if you don't want to maintain UI.

H13.name: Recruiter communication log
H13.description: Per-application log of email/phone/Slack threads with recruiters.

oss_tools.desc: Python IMAP client. Easy to read Gmail. Last commit 2019 — verify before use.
Official Gmail API client. Handles OAuth, search, threads, labels. Right path for Gmail users.
Robust MIME parser — extract body, attachments, headers from raw .eml.

commercial_services.desc: Unified Email/Calendar/Contacts API. Pre-built parsers + threading. Good if you also want calendar.

build_it_yourself.architecture: (1) Gmail API OAuth scope `gmail.readonly` + `gmail.send`; (2) Nightly query: `from:(recruiter@company OR *.greenhouse.io OR *.lever.co)` → list threads; (3) For each application in tracker, fuzzy-match by recruiter email or company domain → link communications table (comm_id, application_id, channel, thread_id, ts, snippet, full_msg_path); (4) Store full body to S3/disk, store snippet + link in DB. Slack: use Slack API `conversations.history` for DM channels. Phone: manual notes UI.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: Gmail API + fuzzy link by recruiter email
recommendation.why: imbox is unmaintained (last commit 2019). Gmail API is the official path and supports labels/threads. Nylas only worth it if you need Outlook support too.

H14.name: Application source tracking
H14.description: Where did you find this job? Referral, LinkedIn, direct, etc.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Single column on applications table: source ENUM [linkedin, linkedin_easy_apply, greenhouse_direct, referral, recruiter_outbound, jobboard_jsearch, jobboard_adzuna, jobboard_usajobs, company_career_page, other]. Add source_url + referrer_person_id (FK to contacts table) when applicable. Drop-down UI populated from the enum. 5-min change to existing schema.

recommendation.why: Trivial column on existing applications table. No external tool needed.

H15.name: Time-in-pipeline alerts
H15.description: Alert if application has been in 'Applied' state >14 days with no response.

oss_tools.desc: Cron job definition + scheduling. Pairs with a simple Python checker script.
In-process scheduler — IntervalTrigger/DateTrigger/CronTrigger. Embeds in your existing Python app.

commercial_services.desc: Dead-man's switch — alerts you if your nightly checker stops running. Pair with cron.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Nightly cron job: `SELECT * FROM applications WHERE status='applied' AND days_since(applied_at) > 14 AND last_activity_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'`. For each result, send alert via configured channels (Telegram bot, email, desktop notification). Add `notifications_sent` table to avoid duplicate alerts. 30 LOC.

recommendation.best_commercial: Healthchecks.io (only for monitoring the cron itself)
recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: nightly SQL query + Telegram bot
recommendation.why: It's a 30-line SQL check + alert sender — no tooling needed beyond a scheduler.

H16.name: Offer deadline tracking
H16.description: When does the offer expire? Countdown + alert before expiry.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Add columns to applications table: offer_received_at, offer_deadline_at, offer_accepted_at. Build alert rules: (T-7d, T-3d, T-1d, T-0d) → send notification. UI badge: '5 days remaining' with color ramp (green→yellow→red). Reuse the same alert sender from H15. ~20 LOC + schema migration.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: deadline_at column + T-7/T-3/T-1/T-0 alert chain
recommendation.why: Two columns + alerting reuse from H15. No external tool.

G13.name: Application confirmation capture
G13.description: Screenshot/email confirmation that you applied, stored in tracker.

oss_tools.desc: page.screenshot(full_page=True) after submission — captures confirmation page directly.

build_it_yourself.architecture: (1) If applying via Playwright: take screenshot immediately after submit click, save as applications/{id}/confirmation_screenshot.png; (2) Save the resulting URL + page text to a 'confirmations' table (application_id, captured_at, source_url, page_text_snippet, screenshot_path); (3) Email confirmation: Gmail API filter `from:(no-reply@company OR careers@*) subject:(application OR received OR confirmation)` → store as HTML + screenshot. UI shows thumbnails of both.
build_it_yourself.estimated_effort: 0.5 day integrated with Playwright apply-bot; 1 day if also pulling email confirmations

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: Playwright screenshot + Gmail API filter
recommendation.why: Two-line Playwright call after every apply submission. Email confirmation is optional but useful for off-bot applications.

G14.name: Withdraw application
G14.description: Mark an application as withdrawn (e.g., accepted another offer).

build_it_yourself.architecture: Add status enum value 'withdrawn' + withdrawn_at timestamp + withdrawn_reason enum [accepted_other_offer, role_no_longer_interesting, salary_misaligned, location_change, other]. Optionally store withdrawal email template + sent_at if you sent a courtesy note. UI: 'Withdraw' button → modal with reason → updates row + sets withdrawn_at. ~30 LOC.

recommendation.why: Status enum + 2 columns. Zero external tooling.

G15.name: Duplicate application prevention
G15.description: Warn if applying to a similar role at the same company you've already applied to.

oss_tools.desc: Reuse from B19. MinHash similarity on JD text → flag pre-apply if sim ≥ 0.85 to existing applications at same company.

build_it_yourself.architecture: Pre-apply check function: `already_applied(company, role_title, jd_text)` → (1) exact match on applications WHERE company_normalized=? AND status != 'rejected' AND (role_title_sim > 0.85 OR jd_minhash_sim > 0.85); (2) Return list of matches with diff view ('You applied to <similar role> on 2025-09-15'). UI: red warning banner with 'Apply anyway' / 'Cancel'. 1 SQL query + 1 minhash compare.

recommendation.best_free_option: Build-it-yourself: pre-apply check using title + minhash similarity vs existing applications
recommendation.why: Same dedup primitive as B19, scoped to your own applications. Reusing avoids double cost.

reuse_opportunities: B19 (cross-time job dedup) and G15 (duplicate application prevention) both use MinHash on JD text — share one datasketch LSH index.
H15 (time-in-pipeline alerts) and H16 (offer deadline alerts) share one alert sender + scheduler.
M19 (rate limiting) and B18 (quota mgmt) both wrap httpx — one transport adapter can do both per-request rate limit + cumulative quota tracking.
M16 (backup) writes to S3; M15 (SOPS+age) encrypts secrets; these compose — `sops exec-env secrets.yaml -- restic backup`.
skip_these_entirely: H14 (source tracking) — single column. Don't over-engineer.
G15 (dup prevention) — reuse B19 minhash. Don't build separately.
cross_cutting_observations.total_build_effort_estimate: ~25-30 dev-days for the entire 19-gap infra stack, assuming single developer and existing tracker DB
